title: Create voice conversation agents · Level 3
slo: Explain how Azure Voice Live supports a real-time spoken conversation agent.

exercises.question_text: What happens between speech-to-text and text-to-speech in a voice conversation?

options.rationale: Recognized text is analyzed or transformed before a response is spoken. This stage can decide what the agent says next.
Uploading can provide audio, but it does not analyze a request or create a response. It is not the middle pipeline stage.
options.better_fit: Use this when an audio file is supplied for recognition.

options.rationale: Voice selection affects the sound of output. It does not determine the response content.
options.better_fit: Use this when choosing how synthesized speech should sound.

options.error_type: Confuses live processing with batch work
options.rationale: Batch scheduling delays work on stored audio. It is not part of the live response-making stage.
options.better_fit: Use this for recordings processed asynchronously.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Processing or reasoning handles recognized text before synthesis.

exercises.question_text: What can the Voice Live API do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The API combines recognition with reasoning and speech synthesis. This reduces separate integration work.
Voice Live can return spoken audio to the user. This enables natural voice conversations.
Voice Live can trigger actions as part of the interaction. It can also support optional avatars.

options.error_type: Confuses managed service with self-managed backend
options.rationale: Azure manages Voice Live models and infrastructure. Developers focus on the conversation experience instead.
options.better_fit: Use this for a solution where the team maintains its own backend components.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Voice Live combines conversation capabilities and can speak or trigger actions.

exercises.question_text: The middle stage of a speech-to-speech pipeline is ___.

parts.text: The middle stage of a speech-to-speech pipeline is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The pipeline would stop at recognition or jump to output without handling the request.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech-to-text comes first and text-to-speech comes last; processing or reasoning sits between them.

exercises.explanation: Processing or reasoning works on recognized text between recognition and speech synthesis.

exercises.question_text: What is Azure Speech Voice Live designed to help build?

options.rationale: Voice Live is designed for agents that listen and respond with spoken audio in real time. It supports live voice conversations.

options.error_type: Confuses Voice Live with batch transcription
options.rationale: Stored-audio transcription is a batch scenario rather than a live conversation. Voice Live focuses on immediate spoken interaction.
options.better_fit: Use this for recordings that need transcription later.

options.error_type: Confuses voice agents with text chat
options.rationale: Text chat does not require voice input or output. Voice Live is intended for spoken interaction.
options.better_fit: Use this when an agent communicates only through written messages.

options.error_type: Confuses managed service with device software
options.rationale: Drivers configure hardware rather than provide conversational AI services. Voice Live manages voice-conversation capabilities.
options.better_fit: Use this when configuring a microphone device.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Voice Live supports live conversational voice agents.

exercises.question_text: Which Voice Live playground options are available? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The playground provides preconfigured samples for quick exploration. Their setup is already supplied.
The playground allows a developer to create a new Voice Live solution. The new solution uses a selected generative AI model.
This option lets the agent initiate the interaction. It changes who starts the conversation.
A new solution requires a generative AI model to be selected. Only a preconfigured sample already has its setup in place.
options.better_fit: Use this only when trying an already configured sample.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The playground offers samples, new solutions, and settings such as proactive engagement.

exercises.question_text: Speech-to-speech requires users to read or type text instead of speaking.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The interaction would no longer be a natural voice conversation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech-to-speech accepts spoken audio and produces spoken audio.

exercises.question_text: Voice mode puts Voice Live speech configuration inside the agent definition.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Speech setup would remain external and require more client-side work.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Voice mode integrates Voice Live into the agent definition, reducing required client code.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Voice mode encapsulates speech configuration in the agent definition.

exercises.question_text: Which extra packages are needed to run a Python Voice Live app? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: pyaudio is listed as a supporting package for the Python Voice Live app. It supports the application's audio handling.
python-dotenv is listed among the required supporting packages. It is part of the stated application setup.
azure-identity is also a listed supporting requirement. It is used alongside the Voice Live package.

options.error_type: Confuses voice requirements with another AI service
options.rationale: This package is not listed as a required supporting package for the Voice Live app. The stated extras are pyaudio, python-dotenv, and azure-identity.
options.better_fit: Use this for image-related Azure AI work.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are the listed supporting packages.

options.text: Takes spoken audio and returns spoken audio
options.rationale: Speech-to-speech begins with a person's voice and ends with a spoken response. Both input and output are audio.

options.text: Takes spoken audio and returns only text
options.rationale: This describes recognition without a spoken reply. It stops at text output.
options.better_fit: Use this for transcription, captions, or dictation.

options.text: Takes text and returns spoken audio
options.rationale: This describes synthesis from written input. It does not understand a person's spoken request.
options.better_fit: Use this when written content must be read aloud.

options.text: Stores recorded audio for later transcription
options.rationale: Saving recordings does not create an immediate spoken exchange. It is not voice input followed by voice output.
options.better_fit: Use this for audio that can be processed later.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech-to-speech is voice in and voice out.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Audio could be played before a response arrived or sent to the wrong destination.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the conversation path from microphone to Voice Live and then from spoken response to speakers.

exercises.correct_answer: Stream microphone audio to Azure Voice Live receive spoken response play it through speakers
exercises.explanation: The application sends microphone audio to Voice Live, receives spoken output, and plays that output through speakers.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the input and output would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the capability first, then identify voice input before voice output.

exercises.correct_answer: Speech-to-speech takes spoken audio as input and produces spoken audio
exercises.explanation: The statement names the capability, then its spoken input, then its spoken output.
